# findOrCreate drops a vanId that matches nothing

**Claim.** Where create echoes a plausible unknown vanId back as a phantom match, findOrCreate just drops it: the ordinary match runs on the rest of the payload — here finding the existing person by name and email — and would have created a person had it found nothing. The vanId only matters when it names a real person.

Applies to: `~1people~1findOrCreate/post`

## Observed exchange

_The person is in the database, under some other vanId._

```http
(setup) POST /people/create

{
  "firstName": "Ignesia",
  "lastName": "Vanidless-{scope}",
  "emails": [
    {
      "email": "ignesia.vanidless-{scope}@example.com"
    }
  ]
}

→ 201
  Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/100000001
{
  "vanId": 100000001,
  "status": "Stored"
}
```

_findOrCreate naming a vanId that exists nowhere, plus their real name and email._

```http
POST /people/findOrCreate

{
  "vanId": 100777777,
  "firstName": "Ignesia",
  "lastName": "Vanidless-{scope}",
  "emails": [
    {
      "email": "ignesia.vanidless-{scope}@example.com"
    }
  ]
}

→ 302
  Location: https://api.securevan.com/v4/people/100000001
{
  "vanId": 100000001,
  "status": "Matched"
}
```
